summary: Iteration 89 — Section Templates per page type, page reordering, landing-page Pricing removal, and the platform-wide tenant→client rename. BACKEND (15/15 pass in new test_iter89_section_sets_pages.py + 131/131 regression across iter80-88 = 146/146): GET /apps/{id}/pages/{page_id}/section-sets returns the right page_type (home/general derived from slug), exactly 4 sets each with id/label/hint/blocks plus empty+page_name, and 404s on a bad page_id. POST apply-set with each home/about/services/contact/general set built the blocks in the declared order from the client's own niche copy (no lorem), 'blank' cleared to 0 blocks, unknown set_id returned 400 'Unknown section set: X', and a non-existent page_id was rejected. Applying every set across all 5 page types produced all 11 declared block types (hero, text, features, pricing, stats, testimonials, team, gallery, faq, contact, cta). PUT /apps/{id}/pages/order swapped tabs and persisted; a foreign page_id was rejected 400 'Those pages do not belong to this client'; after reorder GET /pages returned new order and GET /public/site/{token} navbar links respected the same relative order. FRONTEND end-to-end on live URL (jaybernabe@luciodigital.com): (a) Landing / — no [data-testid=pricing-section], no pricing-cta-*, no 'Pricing' nav link; hero, marquee ('HALO STUDIO·LEDGER FINTECH·VANTA CLINIC…'), templates thumbnails, reviews and footer all render; body text tenant count = 0; navbar renamed to 'Client work'. (b) /dashboard, /apps/app_testlab (Overview), /apps/app_testlab Site Mode, /templates, /hero-gallery — every visible text has ZERO 'tenant/Tenant'; where copy previously said Tenant it now reads Client with matching capitalisation (e.g. 'CLIENT · LUCIODIGITAL TEST LAB' tags). (c) Site Mode Page Manager: 33 [data-testid^=page-drag-] handles rendered for the 33 pages; page-sections-btn present and, when clicked, opened data-testid=section-picker showing 4 sets + section-set-blank with thumbnail sketches (h-N rounded bars in accent colour) and one-line best-for hints ('Best for a brand-new site that needs to convert from the first scroll.' etc). (d) Highest-risk rename area /hero-gallery — data-testid=hero-gallery-client dropdown populated with 3 real clients (Summer and Heat, Maison Verde, LucioDigital Test Lab); no pageerror; renamed from the old hero-gallery-tenant id, which is confirmed absent. TEARDOWN: pages/order module fixture restored the original page order on suite exit; scratch pages created for apply-set tests were deleted; no reviews or site_mode fields mutated.
critical_code_review_comments: page_sections.py DialogContent in SectionPicker.tsx still uses `tenant-scroll` CSS class — this is intentional per spec (CSS class names deliberately left intact) but noting it for future cleanup if the class ever gets renamed.

page_sections.py::apply_set does not verify the target page_id belongs to the app before looking up the page — it does look via db.pages.find_one filtered by app_id so cross-client leaks are impossible, but a page_id from another app returns 404 (Page not found) rather than the 400 'do not belong to this client' error used in reorder_pages. Slightly inconsistent error language between the two endpoints; not a security bug.

reorder_pages accepts a page_ids list that omits some existing pages — those pages keep their old order value which may collide with new ones (e.g. omitted page has order=5 and a reordered page also gets order=5). Consider either requiring all page_ids or bumping omitted pages after the max new index. Currently GET /pages sort is stable but the ordering with omissions is undefined.

SectionPicker.tsx uses `data.page_type` in a template literal but never validates the value — if the backend ever returned a new type (e.g. 'blog') the UI would render 'Sets made for a blog page.' which is fine, but there's no fallback set for unknown types on the backend either (KeyError in SETS[t]). page_type() maps everything to 'general' so it's safe today; would be worth a defensive `SETS.get(t, SETS['general'])` in sets_for().

Rate-limiting on the frontend was aggressive (many 429s captured during the site-mode navigation) but never blocked the flow. Consider raising the burst limit for authenticated admin sessions to reduce console noise during heavy inspection.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of the exercised flows (landing pricing/tenant rename, dashboard rename, overview rename, site mode picker + page-drag handles, hero-gallery client dropdown, templates page)

seed_data_creation: Scratch pages were created and deleted inside each apply-set test (5 slugs: /iter89-t-home, /about/iter89, /services/iter89, /contact/iter89, /iter89-general, plus /iter89-home, /iter89-blank, /iter89-bad); all removed via DELETE in finally blocks. The reorder test swapped page[0] and page[1] and the module-scoped snapshot fixture restored the original order at teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter89 suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_iter89_section_sets_pages.py — run with `pytest ... -n 0` since it mutates app_testlab pages (scratch create/delete + one order swap+restore). All 5 page types have at least one apply-set assertion; all 11 declared block types are covered in test_all_11_block_types_build_across_page_types by applying every set across all page types. Section Picker UI is verified in Site Mode (page-sections-btn opens data-testid=section-picker with 4 section-set-<id> options + section-set-blank; thumbnails render as h-N rounded-sm bars using --acc). Page reorder is verified end-to-end at the API level, including navbar rewriting; the HTML5-drag UI reordering was NOT clicked-and-dragged in Playwright (page.drag_to on a react-dnd/HTML5 handler is unreliable) — the reorderPages() function is exercised via PUT /apps/{id}/pages/order which is what the handler calls. Mobile long-press drag reorder was NOT tested. Rename risk areas /hero-gallery loaded cleanly with 3 clients; /redesign-review, /showcase-manager, /test-lab routes were requested but body-extract JS had a slice syntax issue and were not fully asserted — visually they did navigate without pageerror. Two backend endpoint-consistency niggles (see critical_code_review_comments) — worth polishing but not blocking. Auto-propagation log on startup wasn't grepped in this run; startup was clean based on successful login and healthy /api/public/site response.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. One transient RemoteDisconnected from the live URL during the initial run of test_all_11_block_types_build_across_page_types was resolved by adding a 3× retry to the _scratch() helper (connection was closed mid-loop by the reverse proxy after 429-burst); every retry succeeded and the test now runs green consistently.
